subject: amateur youtube influencers
one_liner: Content supplies in warehouse quantities, for creators with 212 subscribers and a lot of garage space.
brand_voice_notes: Talks like a warehouse club membership desk that has never once questioned whether anyone needs 144 of anything. Unit prices are quoted with pride. Every quantity is too large. Store policy is cited as if it were law. No winking. The staff are friendly and do not care about your channel.

hero.sub: Pallet Club is a members-only warehouse for amateur YouTube influencers. Shocked-face thumbnails by the gross, intros by the pallet, and a 48-pack of "smash that like button" for less than you spent on the ring light.

features.title: The Thumbnail Aisle
features.blurb: 144-count boxes of the same open-mouth face, already pointing at a red arrow. Works out to 0.4 cents per face. You will not use them all. Nobody has.

features.title: Comments, Family Size
features.blurb: "First!", "underrated" and "who's watching in 2027" in 10,000-count drums, shelf-stable for 18 months. Rotate your stock so the engagement doesn't go stale.

features.title: Food Court Collabs
features.blurb: $1.50 gets you a hot dog, a soda and a 40-second collab with whoever is sitting at the next table. They also have a channel. Everyone here has a channel.

testimonials.quote: I bought 2,400 reaction faces in March. I've used nine. The rest are in my garage next to the paper towels and they still look shocked.
testimonials.name: Tanner Oduya
testimonials.title: Unboxing channel, 318 subscribers, four of them cousins

testimonials.quote: The receipt checker at the exit asked what my channel was about and I couldn't answer. He highlighted the receipt anyway. Best feedback I've had all year.
testimonials.name: Brielle Marchetti
testimonials.title: Lifestyle vlogger and full-time assistant manager at a tire shop

testimonials.quote: We filmed a collab at the food court. Neither of us knew the other one was filming. Both versions did about 60 views.
testimonials.name: Dev Kowalczyk
testimonials.title: Gaming streamer, Business Pallet member since last Tuesday

demo_screen_concept: A warehouse aisle browser. A row of hanging aisle signs acts as category tabs (Aisle 1 Thumbnails, Aisle 4 Intros & Outros, Aisle 7 Engagement, Aisle 9 Apologies, Aisle 12 Ring Lights). Below, a grid of bulk products on steel shelving, each with a yellow shelf tag showing pack count, price and unit price per view. Add-to-flatbed updates a running cart total and pallet weight gauge. A featured endcap pallet of shrink-wrapped ring lights sits at the top. A free-sample cart hands out a random b-roll sample. Checkout opens a receipt-check modal where a staff member highlights the receipt and says nothing about your channel.

design_direction.style: Big-box warehouse signage, concrete-floor daylight mode. A membership warehouse club drawn as wayfinding: steel racking, hanging numbered aisle signs, yellow shelf tags with unit prices, and a member card. Vibrant & block-based retail archetype, flat solid fills, type set like signage you read from 40 metres away. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: scorecard grids, stitch seams, pencil annotations, pennants, stud tiles, brass hairlines, crests, velvet ropes, gum leaf corners, sleep rings, zzz chips, 3px ink outlines with hard offset shadows, tennis seams, amount pills, masonry pins, iridescent gradients, lip buttons, lesson paths, wall labels, plinths. Also absent: dark backgrounds, glassmorphism, serif type, paper textures, rounded cards above 3px, handwriting. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The aisle sign: section headings are hung as blue rectangular signs with a big white aisle number on the left and a condensed all-caps category on the right, hanging from two thin grey wires. (2) The shelf tag: every price is a safety-yellow tag with a black top bar, item count, big price and a small 'unit price' line in tabular figures. (3) The pallet beam: orange steel racking beams (#E5711F) run under feature rows and pricing tiers like shelves, with tiny bolt dots. (4) The member card: a red and white card with a bad photo slot and a barcode, used in the hero and the highlighted tier. Corners 3px max. Shadows: none, except a flat 0 6px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.12) under hanging signs.
design_direction.archetype: E-commerce / membership retail landing: hero with member card, aisle-signed feature shelves, testimonials as customer-service desk comment cards, pricing as three membership cards on a rack, footer like a store-hours sign.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Signs swing in from a 3 degree tilt to level on load (200ms ease-out, once). Shelf tags flip up slightly on hover. Add-to-flatbed bumps the cart counter. Receipt highlighter stroke draws across in 400ms. All motion disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left: a hanging aisle sign reading 'AISLE 0 · YOUR CHANNEL', then a huge Anton headline in ink with 'in bulk' in member red, sub copy, red CTA and a yellow shelf tag reading '$60 / yr · unit price $0.16 per day'. Right: a tilted member card (red header band, empty bad-photo slot, barcode, 'GOLD SPECTATOR' tier name, member since 2026) resting on an orange pallet beam. Concrete grey ground with faint floor-tile seams.

images.rationale: Hero skipped: signage style is typographic and the member card carries the hero. Demo product grid uses CSS/SVG packaging, but the featured endcap pallet is photo-shaped, so 1 demo image. Remaining 3 slots on deadpan testimonial headshots of the three named creators.
